memos.risk:
Risk officer view on Pickle ($20 ticket, if the desk buys):

Ticket: $5, the minimum. Pool depth is only 94.6 SOL and the last 15 minutes show heavy two-way churn (sell/buy ~0.94 by SOL), so slippage on exit could eat much of a larger position. Stop: 20%, tight, given the 48.6% drawdown from the 30-minute high and the launch-bot presence. Hold: 15-30 minutes max, since the base-rate edge on post-graduation buys decays fast.

Refuse entirely if: any airdrop or factory signature appears, the bundle share rises further, top-3 concentration climbs, the sell-to-buy ratio stays above 1 on the next check, or the pool drops below roughly 60 SOL. The 26% bundle share and launch bot are yellow flags, and the drawdown means momentum is already broken. My honest lean is to skip this one; the expected edge is weak and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% are a large fraction of the stop distance.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case is thin. Recent flow is roughly balanced: over the last 15 minutes, 183.56 SOL bought against 173.13 SOL sold, with 425 buyers and 362 sellers, and the price is up 14.8% in that window. That is real two-sided activity, not a one-way pump. The curve looks broadly distributed: top-3 buyers hold 10.9% of the curve, top-5 buyers 10.8% of early flow, and the classification is ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen. The coin is alive, and 25.7% above its 30-minute-ago price.

Against that: it is 48.6% off its 30-minute high, a drawdown that suggests the early demand has already faded. Sells nearly matched buys in the first two minutes after graduation (sell/buy ratio 0.91), a launch bot was present, and bundled buyers took 26% of the curve. The pool is shallow at 94.6 SOL, so a $20 round trip would carry meaningful impact and fees.

My verdict: there is no strong case for buying now. The positive signals are modest and the drawdown undercuts the momentum story. I'd recommend SKIP.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: a slow insider or bundle-linked unwind after a sharp dump. The brief shows a 48.6% drawdown from the 30-minute high, while the last 15 minutes still closed +14.8% on a sell-to-buy ratio near 0.94 (173 SOL sold vs 184 bought). That churn looks like profit-taking by early holders, not fresh conviction. Bundled wallets hold 26.3% of the curve, and the completer share of 39% suggests a few buyers carried the graduation. With only 94.6 SOL of pool depth, a $20 ticket faces a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost before any move, and a 30-second execution delay on a coin moving this fast can erase a small bounce. A launch bot was present, and the recent +14.8% may be a relief bounce rather than a trend. Skip.
